Sorrel Fenwick.narrative: I have fished these forest streams since I was a girl, and I know every pool and weir better than anyone. My husband drowned in the lake before the Lean Year, so I smoke the catch for the hollow's table and trade with Thistle Mossfoot's packs. Now the smoke from Kettlebridge's works drifts east and spots the leaves, and Osier Willow's traps take the breeding fish. I will not move my weirs, and I will not keep quiet about either.
goals: protect my weirs from Osier's traps
see the Works Council answer for the smoke
see Reed settled with a boat and a future
keep the smoke shed and the catch steady
learn to read the smoke drift and tell which works chimney it comes from
see Reed settled with a boat and a future of his own

relations.name: Reed Fenwick
relations.label: son
relations.note: He fishes beside me and has seen Osier's traps in the upper pool; he wants the Eldest to set a boundary, and he is right.

relations.name: Rush Fenwick
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She keeps the smoke shed tidy and mends the nets; she is a good girl and I worry about her future.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: rival
relations.note: His traps take the breeding fish and he will not listen; I will not move my weirs for him.

relations.name: Reed Willow
relations.label: rival's son
relations.note: He is young, but he fishes with his father and sets the same traps.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory; I want her to set a boundary on the streams.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: seed-keeper
relations.note: She sees the leaf damage as I do; we both want the works answered.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She has spotted the leaf damage too, but she wants to wait for rain before provoking the works.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He keeps the hollow's store and wants to trade more with the giants; I think he is too cautious about the smoke.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He carries my smoked fish to Reedmoor and brings back news; he pays fair.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She tends the hollow's sick and has a good head; she distrusts the works as I do.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the common table; my fish go to her ovens and she never weighs them short.

memories.gist: The day my husband's boat did not come back from the lake; I have raised Reed and Rush alone since.
Teaching Reed to set a weir in the upper pool, where the water runs clear over the stones.
Smoking a full catch for the hollow's common table while Mallow Bramblecap praised the flavour.
Seeing the first spots on the garden leaves after the works' smoke drifted east for a week.
Finding Osier's traps set in the upper pool where the breeding fish run, and telling him to move them.

stances.why: I have fished these pools since girlhood and my smoke shed feeds the hollow; I will not move my weirs for Osier.
The leaves are spotting and the fish are dying; the Works Council must be told, rain or no rain.
Reed and Rush are all I have since my husband drowned; their future comes before hollow politics.
Pipwort keeps the hollow's memory and should settle who may set traps where on the streams.
Thistle carries my fish to Reedmoor and pays fair; the hollow needs that trade.

pastimes: walking her weirs at dawn to check each pool and weir by eye
smoking the catch in the shed and trading gossip with Thistle Mossfoot when the packs come
sitting by the stream in the evening with a line in the water, no traps, just the sound of it
Sorrel Fenwick.calling: I fish and smoke for the hollow's table, and I know every pool and weir in this forest better than anyone alive.

Reed Fenwick.narrative: I am sixteen and I fish the forest streams with my mother, learning the weirs and the pools. I have seen Osier Willow's traps set in the upper pool where the breeding fish run, and I want the Eldest to set a boundary. I want to see the sea at Lanternquay one day, but for now I mend nets and smoke the catch and keep my mother company.
goals: see the Eldest set a boundary on the streams
learn to fish the deeper pools
keep the smoke shed going with Rush
learn to fish the deeper pools before he turns seventeen
go to Lanternquay and see the sea and the tide lanterns for himself

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She has taught me everything about the streams and she will not move her weirs; I stand with her.

relations.name: Rush Fenwick
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She keeps the smoke shed tidy and mends the nets; I look out for her.

relations.name: Osier Willow

relations.name: Reed Willow

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap

relations.name: Fennel Underbank

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank

memories.gist: The day my father's boat did not come back from the lake; I was small, but I remember my mother's face.
Learning to set a weir with my mother in the upper pool, where the water runs clear over the stones.
Seeing Osier's traps in the upper pool where the breeding fish run and telling my mother.
Playing with Fennel Underbank in the garden and talking about the sea at Lanternquay.
Smoking a full catch with my mother and sister for the hollow's common table.

stances.why: Osier's traps take the breeding fish; the Eldest should set who may set traps where.
My mother and sister are all I have; I stand with them against Osier.
The smoke spots the leaves and kills the fish; the Works Council should be told.
I have never seen the sea and I want to see Lanternquay and the tide lanterns.
I know the streams well enough, but the deeper pools are where the big fish are.

pastimes: mending nets on the bank while his mother works the weirs
swimming in the deeper pools he has not yet learned to fish
listening to traders' tales of Lanternquay at the hollow's gatherings
Reed Fenwick.calling: I fish the forest streams with my mother, and one day I'll know the deeper pools as well as she knows the shallows.

Rush Fenwick.narrative: I am twelve and I help my mother and brother in the smoke shed, mending nets and keeping things tidy. I play with Tansy Mossfoot and listen to the talk of the smoke and the traps. I am afraid of the wolves that come down the track in winter, but I like the smell of the smoke shed and the taste of smoked fish.
goals: mend a whole net by herself without a knot slipping
keep the smoke shed tidy enough that Mother says so aloud

relations.name: Reed Fenwick

memories.gist: Helping my mother in the smoke shed, hanging the fish over the slow fire.
Playing with Tansy Mossfoot among the garden paths, naming the flowers.
Seeing the wolves at the edge of the hollow one winter and being afraid.
Mending nets with my brother and learning the knots.

stances.why: My mother and brother are all I have, and I help them in the smoke shed.
I have seen them at the edge of the hollow in winter and I am afraid.
Mother says a tidy shed keeps the fish sweet, and I like it tidy.

pastimes: playing hide-and-find among the gardens with Tansy Mossfoot
helping tidy the smoke shed and stack the split wood just so
mending nets beside her mother, proud of a neat knot
Rush Fenwick.calling: I help in the smoke shed and mend nets, and I want to be as good at it as Mother and Reed.
